title: How I work
introduction: Starting by reading the land, sensing the relationships that shape it and finding ways to translate them into culinary creations to share.
diagramDescription: Perceiving relationships sits at the centre of a circle describing the connections between the material, the living and the cultural. Territory branches into Matter and Knowledge; one route continues towards Experience and the other towards Transformation. Both meet at Sharing. Finer lines connect the central circle to each domain. Each drawing links to its step in the process.

nodes.title: Territory
nodes.description: Mountains, sun, rivers and air. Soil, climate, aromas, ecosystems, culture, producers and seasons give context to the ingredients.

nodes.title: Matter
captionLines: and the ecosystem they belong to.
nodes.description: Understand its character, cycles and role in the ecosystem. Roots and leaves connect water, soil, air and light: an image of photosynthesis and life.

nodes.title: Knowledge
nodes.description: Observe, try, remember and try again. Bring together experience, research, botany, traditional knowledge, cultivation, gathering, technique and sensory analysis.

nodes.title: Transformation
captionLines: The technique at the service of the product.
nodes.description: Macerate, distil, extract, ferment, concentrate, combine and preserve. Choose the gesture that expresses the character of the ingredient.

nodes.title: Experience
captionLines: in the body and through time.
nodes.description: The result becomes sensation: aroma, flavour, temperature, texture and persistence. It awakens memories and opens new questions.

nodes.title: Sharing
nodes.description: Five hands hold a single thread that connects them. The essence lies in encounter, community, collaboration and the exchange of knowledge. Sharing gives meaning to the creation.
